sulfonylation of propargyl esters with sulfonyl
hydrazides
Zhi-Xiong Ou, Bu-Hong Zhang, Jia-Xin Song, Li-Bo Li and Xing-Wang Wang *
rsc.li/obc
Palladium-catalyzed enantioselective propargylic sulfonylation
between racemic propargyl esters and readily available sulfonyl
hydrazides with an N-benzylamino-bridged bidentate phosphora-
midite (N-Bn-Me-BIPAM) ligand was reported. The corresponding
reactions provided a series of enantiomerically rich propargylic
sulfones in good yields with high enantioselectivity under mild
reaction conditions.
1. Introduction

\left( \mathbf { R } { - } \mathbf { S } \mathbf { O } _ { 2 } { - } \mathbf { R } \right)
backbones endowed with distinct electronic
and structural features are versatile synthetic intermediates in
organic chemistry.<sup>1</sup> As a result, sulfone compounds were
widely found in many target molecules of importance in syn-
thetic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, agricultural chemistry,
and materials science.<sup>2</sup> The sulfone moiety enhances the
eficacy and potency of a drug molecule by forming strong
hydrogen bonds with a biological target.<sup>3</sup> Therefore, sulfones
not only serve as important building blocks in numerous
medicines and drug candidates and natural products, but also
play important roles in the discovery of new anticancer agents,
antibacterial agents, insecticides and herbicides.<sup>4</sup> In the past
few decades, great progress has been made in the synthesis of
sulfonyl compounds, and a variety of novel organo- and metal-
catalyzed methods have been established.<sup>5</sup> Among these
methods, the development of eficient and practical synthetic
methods for chiral sulfones has attracted significant interest
from synthetic chemists.<sup>6</sup>
Alkynyl sulfones are sulfone derivatives that show very
important synthetic utility and are crucial structural moieties
that are present in some pharmaceutically and biologically active
molecules, such as the inhibitors of cathepsins, cancer Osaka
thyroid kinase modulators, DNA cleaving agents, etc. (Fig. 1).<sup>7</sup>

increased attention due to the increase in use,<sup>8</sup> and correspond-

complex-catalyzed asymmetric transformation for the syn-

enantioselectivity, highlighting the potential utility of this syn-
thetic method (Scheme 1d).

3. Conclusions
In summary, palladium-catalyzed enantioselective sulfonyla-
tion of propargyl carbonates with sulfonyl hydrazides that uti-
lizes a chiral N-Bn-Me-BIPAM ligand under mild reaction con-
ditions was developed. This reaction delivered the corres-
ponding propargyl sulfones in good yields with high enantio-
selectivity. Meanwhile, this transformation has good func-
tional group tolerance, a wide substrate scope, as well as good
atom and step economy. It is noteworthy that the employment
of air as a promoter ensures the reactivity and delivers optimal
catalytic results. Further eforts in our laboratory are focused
on expanding the stereoselective transformation of propargyl
carbonates into a practical catalytic system.
